sections.html:
The Register of Deeds sits at 355 N. Belvedere Drive, Suite 201, Gallatin, TN 37066. Phone 615-452-3892, fax 615-442-1105. The counter serves the public Monday through Friday from 8:00 to 4:30.

Down the hall are the Assessor of Property (Room 206) and the Trustee (Room 107). That means value and tax questions can be answered during the same visit as your recording.

In a typical fiscal year the office records more than 30,000 legal documents across over eighty types of instrument (see the county page), so routine home sales are familiar work for the staff.

Gallatin is the seat of a county of eight cities, roughly 25 miles northeast of Nashville. The others are Hendersonville, Goodlettsville, Millersville, Mitchellville, Portland, Westmoreland and White House. Population was 215,538 in July 2025, a 9.8% gain over April 2020, spread over 89,138 housing units of which 72.0% are owner-occupied. The 2020 to 2024 median value for an owner-occupied home is $393,100, and a typical owner with a mortgage pays $1,831 a month. Permits for 3,045 buildings were issued in 2025. Because prices run high, transfer tax is a real expense at closing, and your title company can give you the figure early.

Go to ustitlesearch.net to search records certified from September 1989 forward. Older material, deed books and indexes as far back as 1786, has been digitized as well, so you can follow an old chain of title from your couch. Prefer paper? A public search room is open at the office.

MyLandAlert is a free fraud monitor the register operates with ProGResS, Inc. You get an email the moment anything is recorded in your name or your business's name, a quick tip-off to a forged deed or mortgage fraud. Owners of rentals, vacant lots and inherited houses benefit most, because nobody is watching those properties daily. If an alert arrives for a document you do not recognize, phone the register at 615-452-3892 and ask what was filed. A sale-ready owner should also set up the alert before listing, so a forged filing cannot surface in the middle of a contract.

The office accepts e-recorded deeds through Simplifile, Inc. and CSC eRecording Solutions, and documents are received, recorded and returned faster than with paper. Tennessee restricts electronic submission to professionals such as attorneys, lenders and title companies, so a seller typically depends on whoever is handling the sale.

Paper still works. Deliver or mail the notarized, signed original to Suite 201 together with the fees. Because fees depend on the document, call 615-452-3892 for the exact recording fee before you send it.

Staff take in the recording fees plus two state taxes, transfer and mortgage, when a document is filed. Each month the tax money is sent to the Department of Revenue, while the county keeps the fees. The state rates:

State recordation taxes collected at the register
TaxRate
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of purchase price
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exempt

Who covers the tax is spelled out in your purchase contract. State law exempts certain transfers, among them an executor's deed under a will and a deed from a divorce settlement. When the buyer borrows, mortgage tax is paid on the lender's deed of trust. The release of your own paid-off loan is recorded once closing is done.

What a recordable deed contains is set by Tennessee Code. Expect to see:

  • Names of grantor and grantee, with a legal description
  • Derivation clause that names the earlier recorded deed
  • Name and address of the owner and the tax payer, and of the preparer
  • Parcel number, plus a sworn statement of value if the deed is taxable
  • Notarized acknowledgment of the signature

Drafting and legal advice are outside the staff's role, and a deed that lacks an item may be refused. Attorneys and title companies generally verify this list for you.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
Take the notarized original deed and enough payment for recording and any state tax. If there is a lender, the title company commonly sends the deed of trust along with it. Gather three details in advance, since the deed uses each: the Assessor's parcel number, how the prior deed was recorded, and where the tax bill should be mailed.

After recording, the document is scanned into the database for online viewing. Store the recorded copy with your closing papers, as lenders and buyers sometimes ask later for its instrument number. Spot a misspelled name or a wrong parcel number? Report it to your closing agent promptly so a correcting document can be prepared and recorded.

sections.h2: Step by step for a seller
sections.html:
A typical sale moves through this office in a few moves. The deed is prepared by your title company or attorney and checked against the list above, then you sign in front of a notary. The original reaches the register by e-recording or on paper at Suite 201, and staff index it, take the tax and fees, and enter it in the database.

Recording fees are small compared with the tax. If the house came to you through a will or a divorce, ask whether the transfer is one of the exempt types before the deed is drawn, since that changes what your closing agent must collect.

When in doubt that a document can be recorded as written, call 615-452-3892 before mailing. A question costs less than a returned packet. Mailed packets should include the original deed, a check or money order that covers recording and tax, and a note with your phone number so staff can reach you about a missing item. Keep a photocopy of everything you send for your own files.

sections.h2: Is the house really in Sumner County?
sections.html: Not always. Goodlettsville partly lies in Davidson County, and Millersville, Portland and White House each stretch into Robertson County. A Sumner city name on the mail therefore says little about the parcel's county. Verify with the Assessor's property search or the parcel number on the deed before choosing a register, and ask the title company where the filing goes.

Recording puts a new name on the record but pays no tax. The county bill is due the first Monday in October and goes delinquent after February 28. Call the Trustee, 615-452-1260, for the parcel balance before you close, and give the Assessor, 615-452-2412, the new owner's mailing address.

Agree on the order of events with your closing agent. Balance first, then signing and notarizing, then filing, then the scan appearing in the database. With a cash buyer there is no deed of trust and no mortgage tax, so the packet is shorter.

faqs.q: What are the Sumner County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The counter is open weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30, in Suite 201 at 355 N. Belvedere Drive in Gallatin. Phone 615-452-3892.
Yes, using Simplifile, Inc. or CSC eRecording Solutions. In practice the title company handling your sale files for you.

faqs.q: How far back do Sumner County online records go?
faqs.a: Certified records start in September 1989 and are searchable online, and digitized deed books and indexes reach back to 1786.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Sumner County sale?
faqs.a: $0.37 for each $100 of purchase price, paid at recording. Your title company can compute the exact amount for your deal.

faqs.q: Can I get alerts about filings under my name in Sumner County?
faqs.a: Yes. MyLandAlert costs nothing and sends an email once a document is recorded under your name or business.
